extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) provides two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification systems), the provider may choose internal control or notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied; Annex VII (notified body) assessment is described as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems in some sources.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII conformity assessment procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the Article 43 conformity assessment procedure, authorising placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited time, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Annex VII, point 4.5, provides that notified bodies may be granted access to training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, when necessary to assess conformity and after other reasonable means have proven insufficient, subject to a reasoned request and existing IP/confidentiality law.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts updating Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.

A Council document (7322/26) references a designation scope system for conformity assessment bodies notified under 'Article 30' of 'this Regulation,' listing AI system categories (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) tied to Annex I of the AI Act, suggesting a related/companion regulatory framework for designation of AI conformity assessment bodies.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories of AI systems for the NANDO information system, used for notification and designation of conformity assessment bodies, and proposes amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are medical-device-specific designations, not AI Act-specific designations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device-related AI systems.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across member states and limited capacity.

Post-2026, Notified Bodies designated specifically under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, which will intersect with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments for medical device AI.
The high-risk AI obligations under the AI Act were originally expected to fully apply in August 2026, according to a 2026 compliance guide.

A September 2026 news source reports that the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations has been moved to 2 August 2029, replacing an earlier date of 2 December 2027, due to harmonised standards and notified bodies not being ready.

A September 22, 2026 source states that under a 'second amendment' to Article 113 of the AI Act, Annex III high-risk obligations (e.g., AI in hiring, education, credit scoring, essential services) now apply from 2 August 2029, replacing the 2 December 2027 date set by the 'AI Omnibus,' and that until then providers do not need a notified body conformity assessment for these systems.

A September 29, 2026 client alert confirms that EU institutions have deferred high-risk Annex III requirements to 2 August 2029, citing the need for providers/deployers to wait for harmonised standards and the designation of the first notified bodies.

Separately, under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in the Commission's NANDO database for the CRA, with a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application from 11 December 2027.

The Article 43 text in the 2022 proposal version required providers of high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III to opt for one of two conformity assessment procedures when relying on harmonised standards or common specifications.

contradictions.claim_a: The EU moved the start date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations to 2 August 2029, replacing the 2 December 2027 date, due to lack of readiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.
contradictions.claim_b: An April 2026-referenced compliance guide states that 'August 2026: High-risk AI obligations fully apply' as 'the key deadline for medical device AI,' with notified bodies designated under the AI Act expected only post-2026.
contradictions.description: Sources disagree on the application date for high-risk AI Act obligations: later 2026 news sources (15, 20, 26) state the deadline was deferred to 2 August 2029, while source 24 describes August 2026 as the date when high-risk obligations 'fully apply,' reflecting outdated or conflicting information given the dates of publication.

contradictions.claim_a: As of March 2026, notified body designation under the AI Act is ongoing but the 'August 2026 deadline isn't moving.'
contradictions.claim_b: By September 2026, multiple sources report that the deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations has been moved to 2 August 2029.
contradictions.description: Source 22 (published around March 2026) asserts the August 2026 deadline is fixed and not moving, while later September 2026 sources (15, 20, 26) report that the deadline was in fact moved to August 2029, indicating source 22 is outdated relative to subsequent regulatory changes.

open_issues: No source provides a definitive, authoritative list of notified bodies specifically designated under the EU AI Act (as opposed to MDR/IVDR or CRA), leaving unclear exactly how many, if any, AI Act-specific notified bodies have been designated as of October 2026.

It is unclear from the sources how the Council document (7322/26) and Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) referencing 'Article 30' designation scope and a new 'Annex XIV' NANDO framework relate procedurally to Article 43/Annex VII of the AI Act — whether these constitute adopted law, pending proposals, or amendments, and their current legislative status is not clarified.

The exact legislative instrument and date of the alleged 'second amendment' to Article 113 extending the Annex III deadline to 2 August 2029 is not documented via an official EU source (e.g., Official Journal or EUR-Lex), only via news/blog sources of September 2026, leaving its formal adoption status unconfirmed.

The relationship and timeline alignment between the original December 2027 deadline, the newly reported August 2029 deadline, and the earlier August 2026 'full application' date cited in some industry sources is not reconciled by any single authoritative source.

It is unclear from the sources exactly which notified bodies (if any) have received formal AI Act designation as of October 2026, and whether the NANDO system has begun listing AI Act-specific entries distinct from MDR/IVDR/CRA designations.

The practical interplay between MDR/IVDR notified body assessments and new AI Act-specific conformity assessments for medical device AI (SaMD) is described only at a high level, without detail on whether a single notified body audit can cover both frameworks or whether separate audits are required.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems built around internal control or notified body assessment, though the underlying sources describing this basic Article 43 structure are themselves rated only low confidence due to limited authority and corroboration (low confidence) ([Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). By contrast, the requirement that systems already covered by sectoral EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I, Section A)—such as medical devices and machinery—follow sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements, is well-supported (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). Significant uncertainty surrounds both the current designation status of AI Act-specific notified bodies and the applicable compliance deadlines, with multiple contradictory reports emerging in 2026 about timeline extensions.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 is reported to provide two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment by a notified body of the quality management system and technical documentation under Annex VII, though this characterization rests on lower-authority sources (low confidence) ([Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I, Section A)—such as medical devices and machinery—providers must follow the sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

For biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1, the choice between internal control and notified body assessment reportedly depends on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, though some sources describe notified body assessment as mandatory for this category (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)).

Providers generally may choose any notified body, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use—in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43 (GA)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally require a new conformity assessment, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment for limited periods on public security, health, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies, in limited circumstances, to access training data and trained models when necessary for assessment (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these designations are medical-device-specific and not AI Act-specific (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex evaluation document](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device-related AI systems (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)), and as of March 2026 the notified body ecosystem was still being built across member states with limited capacity (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). Separately, a Council document and a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) reference a new "Annex XIV" NANDO framework and "Article 30" designation scope system, suggesting a related but unclear regulatory mechanism for designating AI conformity assessment bodies (medium confidence) ([Council doc 7322/26](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf), [COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources conflict sharply on the applicable deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations. # Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems: internal control or notified body assessment, with the applicable route depending on the system's category and existing sectoral regulation (high confidence). However, significant uncertainty surrounds both the current designation status of AI Act-specific notified bodies and the applicable deadlines for compliance, with multiple contradictory reports emerging in 2026 about timeline extensions.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 provides two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment by a notified body of the quality management system and technical documentation under Annex VII (low confidence) ([Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I, Section A)—such as medical devices and machinery—providers must follow the sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

For biometric identification systems under Annex III point 1, the choice between internal control and notified body assessment depends on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, though some sources describe notified body assessment as mandatory for this category (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)).

Providers generally may choose any notified body, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use—in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43 (GA)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally require a new conformity assessment, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard conformity assessment for limited periods on public security, health, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII point 4.5 allows notified bodies, in limited circumstances, to access training data and trained models when necessary for assessment (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these designations are medical-device-specific and not AI Act-specific (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex evaluation document](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Sources conflict sharply on the applicable deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations. Some 2026 sources assert full application in August 2026 (low confidence) ([MDxCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)), while later September 2026 news sources claim the deadline was moved to 2 August 2029, replacing an earlier 2 December 2027 date, due to unready harmonised standards and notified bodies (low confidence, all below 0.4) ([EU AI Act Legal Guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [AI Law Insights](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply), [Tech Legal Alerts](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline)). ## Knowledge Gaps
